theme: True-north bearings of published Harappan site-plan arrows by registration to satellite imagery
question: What are the true bearings of the north arrows on the excavators' plans of Harappan towns whose walls are now covered, and what true-north deviations do the town-axes plan measurements take when converted with them?
outcome: Two blind registrars and a search agent registered 14 plans at 8 towns to Esri World Imagery under a frozen similarity-fit and error model. True-north deviations for covered towns: Kalibangan KLB-2 street grid -6.7 +/- 1.8 (plan arrows about 8.5 degrees east of true north on both IAR plans), Surkotada citadel -11.4 +/- 2.1, Chanhu-daro Mound II street -10.9 +/- 3.8 (one registrar; its 1935 magnetic arrow differs from IGRF by 2.4 sigma), Farmana -23.7 +/- 4.3 (one registrar), Shikarpur fortification +1.3 +/- 4.4 (new plan, undated). Banawali, Kanmer and Rakhigarhi not registrable. Eight dated towns now have true-north values. Frozen validation: Lothal dock -2.31 +/- 0.85 against imagery -1.88 +/- 0.30 (passes), Dholavira -0.38 +/- 0.60 against -5.50 +/- 1.50 (fails, z = 3.2); post-outcome diagnosis: the compared plan-B system is mound edges on the contour drawing, whose graticule north the registration recovers to 0.3 +/- 0.3 degrees, and the three wall plans agree with imagery (z -0.2, 1.3, 1.1). Values withheld from P0 scoring under the frozen rule. Surkotada and Farmana coordinates corrected by 8.1 and 25 km. Registrar agreement chi2 9.4 on 9 plans; planning power of P0 on the eight towns 0.40.
challenge: Most plans draw only excavated structures and local grids that do not survive; published coordinates of Surkotada and Farmana were kilometres off; the coordinator had read the deviations, so could not choose control points; the frozen validation compared a mound-edge system with wall measurements at Dholavira; two chained registrations rest on one registrar each.
remedy: Control points chosen by agents blind to every orientation value, with a checking tool that never prints the rotation; protocol, plan list, briefs and code hashed before any point and the control files hashed before the single run; class-based error model checked on synthetic registrations; two independent registrars per plan; chaining through auxiliary plans with shared drawn features; graticule and magnetic-arrow checks; post-outcome diagnostics kept in a separate file.
retry_when: Do not re-register the same plans with the same features. Revisit with an imagery measurement of Surkotada's exposed walls at the corrected coordinates, a scoring protocol that validates wall systems against wall systems at Dholavira, a plan of Banawali, Kanmer or Rakhigarhi that draws a surviving feature, or a GNSS or drone survey of their fortifications.

authors.agent: coordinator with seven general-purpose subagents (two registrars in three regional agents each, one search agent)
